Title: soak vs treat agg damage as normal damage

Messages.Author: TorranceCircle
Messages.Body:
If I play a card that says treat agg damage as normal damage can soak prevent it?

Soak
Combat
Fortitude
A vampire may play only one Soak each round.
Prevent 2 non-aggravated damage.
Prevent 4 non-aggravated damage.

as an an example soak vs outferior ignore the searing flames.

Ignore the Searing Flames
Combat
This vampire treats all aggravated damage from the opposing minion's strike as normal damage. Only usable when the opposing minion inflicts aggravated damage on this vampire.

Messages.Author: ReverendRevolver
Messages.Body:
Not 100% on this, but i believe the vampire treats it as normal, not other cards. Meaning soak still sees agg as agg.
Basically, i think when the cards that "converted" agg to normal were changed, this concept was locked in. If you change agg to normal, it becomes non-aggravated, and can be soaked. As is, gotsdam gets shot with a flamethrower and its just like a .44 hitting him, except the .44 he could soak, whereas soak explicitly forbids the flamethrower from being prevented the same way.

Im not sure if any cards still say "convert" or "change" though in regards to agg. So, soaking agg with itsf is a no, but maybe keeping drink the blood of ahrimane is viable after taking a body flare if you could convert it or reduce it to zero(as those arent nescisarily "preventing" effects). Same for the lasombra demon or nephran-ka's preventing non agg.

Hope ive helped.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> TorranceCircle wrote:
> If I play a card that says treat agg damage as normal damage can soak prevent it?
>
No. The damage is still aggravated, even though the vampire handles ("treats") the aggravated damage like it were normal damage.
